en: You can build single-page applications with
Next.js,
even though you're technically building a
full-stack
application. And
that might sound confusing, and it's also
not what we've built thus far, essentially,
you could say.
Because thus far, we used server-side
routing to
load different pages and load different
content, and we used HTMX to
update update those loaded pages upon
certain user actions.
And whilst this is one way of using HTMX and
a pretty popular way, I should say, it's not
the only one. And for that, I prepared a
brand new project which you find attached
and therefore you should download it and run
npm install in that downloaded project
snapshot so that you have all the
dependencies. And then npm start to start
the development server.
And what you'll have here in this project is
essentially a basic shop website
where you can click on products to be taken
to the detail pages.
Not too fancy, but pretty easy to
understand, I'd say.
Now, this site is still a full-stack website
where the routing happens on the server. I
got 2 main routes here on my server,
one for loading all the products or the page
with all the products and one for loading a
page with the product details.
And both of these routes return a complete
HTML document as you can tell.
Now, as you can also see, I'm already
loading HTMX into my pages here because HTMX
can actually also be used to navigate
between these 2 pages
without forcing a full page reload. Because
at the moment where I load HTMX but I'm not
using it, since I don't have any HTMX
attributes anywhere in my code here,
at the moment without HTMX, if you watch
that refresh icon here, if I click a
product, you see it briefly changes to a
cross.
Also, if I go back,
And that is always a sign that a brand new
page was requested from the server and was
loaded onto the screen.
So the browser navigated from the old page
to the new page. And there's nothing wrong
with that, but that's now not a single page
application, it's a multi-page application
instead.
And we do navigate around here because these
products are wrapped in anchor tags, for
example. So we got these links here.
And whilst that works, we can now also use
HTMX for that navigation,
which basically means that we use HTMX to
send this request to the next page behind
the scenes
and that it should then take the response.
So here, this entire response for the
product details page, for example,
and replace the currently loaded page's DOM
with the new page's DOM. DOM that should be
rendered for that next page so that we
technically never leave the current page.
We just replace all the rendered content
with the content of the next page. That's
how single-page applications work and that
can also be implemented with HTMX.
